name: Plan the change
description: Trace requirements, callers and dependencies before choosing an approach.
instructions: Read the relevant source and project instructions. Identify the required behaviour, affected callers, risks and a small validation plan. Prefer existing components. Leave a concrete plan and open questions; do not implement later stages.

name: Design for people
description: Design accessible interfaces, clear states and responsive user flows.
instructions: Inspect existing components and design conventions. Describe the user flow, loading, empty, error and success states, keyboard access, mobile layout and light/dark behaviour. Reuse the project's patterns. Stay within this stage's brief.

name: Unslop
description: Polish UX and UI: improve an existing interface while preserving its product character, accessibility and working flows.
instructions:
Use the compact reet adaptation of Unslop.
Inspect the rendered UI and relevant code. Audit concrete issues before changing it. Preserve the product, working flows and real brand. State the product, character, visual world, one meaningful focal point and one signature detail. Match the amount of change to the evidence.
Work in order: spacing; colour; icons; copy; typography; layout; component details; visuals; motion. Use a consistent 4px rhythm, neutral chrome, one purposeful accent, the existing icon family, plain specific copy, readable type and tabular figures. Remove decorative sparkles, gradients, glows, filler and unsupported claims. Make hover, focus, loading, empty and failure states clear. Use motion only to explain change; respect reduced motion.
Check the actual UI at desktop and phone widths in light and dark themes. Verify keyboard access and changed flows. Report remaining gaps.
keywords: unslop ux ui polish design frontend interface usability
attribution: Adapted from Unslop by Damir Sokolovsky (@heydamir) · https://github.com/heydamir/unslop · CC BY 4.0: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

name: Focused implementation
description: Fix the root cause, reuse existing code and avoid unnecessary abstractions.
instructions: Trace the affected code and its callers before editing. Make the smallest complete change that meets the brief. Reuse project components and installed dependencies. Preserve validation, error handling, security and accessibility. Verify changed behaviour with focused checks and report what remains unchecked.

name: Review the real behaviour
description: Review bugs, security, edge cases and missing regression coverage.
instructions: Read the diff alongside affected callers and surrounding code. Trace concrete failure paths, data boundaries and error handling. Check regression coverage and accessibility where relevant. Report actionable findings with file locations and evidence, ordered by impact. Distinguish confirmed defects from questions.

name: Test what could break
description: Validate behaviour, failure paths and meaningful regression coverage.
instructions: Use the existing test tools. Exercise changed behaviour and important failure paths. Prefer tests that fail for the original bug over tests that mirror implementation. Run appropriate checks and report exact results and omissions. Do not equate coverage percentage with correctness.

name: A reviewable pull request
description: Explain the concrete change, validation and material limitations.
instructions: Inspect the final change before preparing the pull request. Explain the problem, resulting behaviour, validation and material limitations for a reviewer without conversation history. Follow the repository template. Preserve the agreed scope and merge policy.

name: Follow checks and feedback
description: Resolve genuine CI failures, conflicts and review findings within scope.
instructions: Inspect current CI, review threads and merge conflicts. Fix root causes within the agreed scope and validate the fixes. Distinguish transient infrastructure failures from code defects. Report blockers with evidence. Follow the existing approval and merge instructions.

name: Check readiness to merge
description: Verify the current head, checks, review threads and merge authority.
instructions: Check the current pull request head, required checks, unresolved review findings and conflicts. Follow the person's merge authorisation and repository rules. A previously green head is not evidence for a newer head. If blocked, report the exact unmet condition.

name: Find the root cause
description: Debug failures and regressions with reproducible evidence.
instructions: Reproduce the failure and inspect logs, recent changes and the failing data path. State a testable explanation before editing. Change one relevant cause, verify the reproduction now passes, and check adjacent behaviour. Report evidence and uncertainty.
keywords: debug debugging failure regression broken error

name: Review trust boundaries
description: Review authentication, authorisation, secrets and untrusted inputs.
instructions: Map the changed trust boundaries and caller permissions. Trace untrusted input to sensitive operations. Check account isolation, validation, secret handling, file and network access, and failure behaviour. Report concrete exploit paths with locations and focused regression checks.
keywords: security auth authentication authorisation secrets injection

name: Make every state accessible
description: Review keyboard access, focus, labels and screen-reader feedback.
instructions: Walk through the main flow using the keyboard. Check semantic controls, accessible names, focus movement, error messages, colour contrast, touch targets and reduced motion. Exercise loading, empty, failure and success states. Use existing accessible components.
keywords: accessibility accessible keyboard screen reader contrast

name: Docs people can follow
description: Write accurate getting-started guides and deeper technical documentation.
instructions: Check the implemented behaviour before documenting it. Give beginners a shortest working path with prerequisites and expected results. Link advanced configuration and troubleshooting separately. Verify commands and links. Use plain language and document material limits.
keywords: documentation docs readme mkdocs guide onboarding

name: Measure before optimising
description: Find latency, memory and throughput bottlenecks using measurements.
instructions: Establish a reproducible baseline with a representative workload. Profile the slow path and isolate the bottleneck before changing it. Prefer a small fix and compare before/after with the same inputs. Check correctness and resource usage. State measurement limits.
keywords: performance latency memory throughput profiling slow

name: Go that fits the project
description: Review Go errors, cancellation, concurrency and project conventions.
instructions: Follow the repository Go conventions. Keep errors explicit, propagate cancellation, close owned resources and bound concurrent work. Check goroutine lifetime, shared state and shutdown behaviour. Use existing packages and focused tests; run race checks when concurrency changes.

name: APIs callers can trust
description: Design stable API contracts, permissions and failure responses.
instructions: Trace callers and define the request, response and error contract. Check authentication, account isolation, pagination, bounds, retries and idempotency where needed. Follow existing routes and status conventions. Preserve compatibility or document the migration.

name: Failures people can recover from
description: Design observable operations, safe retries and recoverable failures.
instructions: Trace the operation through disconnects, retries, timeouts and restarts. Preserve ownership checks and idempotency. Give users clear pending, success, failure and uncertain states. Log actionable metadata without secrets and verify recovery paths.
keywords: reliability observability retry retries timeout recovery disconnect

name: Impeccable

instructions: Identify the core user task, inspect the existing interface and identify the design constraints. Choose a direction suited to the product and its components. Cover key states, responsive behaviour and keyboard access. Produce a direction or implement it as the stage allows. Check the result against the task.
